corrections.text: The article says The Register "says the legacy backend will be removed in the 2.16 release". The Register's sentence is conditional: "if the new NCCL backend works as expected, the older version will be removed in the 2.16 release, planned for early next year." The PyTorch 2.15 release notes state the removal without that condition ("will be removed in the next release").

The article says The Register's "One process group gets only one communicator during initialization" and the release notes' per-peer-pair communicators for nccl-lazy "differ in scope; neither explains the difference". The Register states its rule for initialization and "by default", and the release notes say nccl-lazy runs collectives on one eagerly created communicator while per-peer-pair communicators are created lazily; the cited sources do not show the two accounts to conflict.
